name: stage-depth-quantise
summary: a generic stage of mocha-stage: every sample of each frame snapped to the values of an 8 bit or 16 bit integer grid with the pixel-format crate, by a conversion to that depth and back; the stream keeps its depth; a published method under explicit configuration, not compared with any product

binaries.name: mocha-stage
binaries.arguments: apply depth-quantise --width W --height H --depth 8|16|32 --fps N[/D] [--frames N] [--describe] [--param K=V]...
binaries.stdin: whole raw frames; not read with --describe
binaries.stdout: the frames of the stage, nothing else; with --describe one line of JSON
binaries.stderr: empty on exit 0; exactly one line error: CODE: MESSAGE on a failure

frame_contract: frames/2 raw frames: depth 8 is packed rgba (4 bytes per pixel), depth 16 is packed rgba64le (8 bytes), depth 32 is planar gbrapf32le (16 bytes, planes G, B, R, A, 1.0 is full scale); whole frames back to back, no header, no padding, straight alpha, a frame of at most 4 GiB; a stream that ends inside a frame is a partial frame

parameters.maps_to: The integer depth of the grid the samples are snapped to.
The integer that stands for full scale on the 16 bit grid (Config::u16_max); read when levels is 16.
How a real number becomes an integer (Config::rounding).
The floating point type of the arithmetic (Config::precision).
What happens to a rounded value outside the grid or to a value that is not a number (Config::clamp).

geometry: preserve: the output has the width, height, depth, rate and frame count of the input; --describe answers the geometry of the request
sample_rule: computed on bit patterns: an 8 or 16 bit sample is its integer, with full scale 255 or 65535, and a depth 32 sample is the bits of its float; the stage itself neither clamps nor rounds, the rules of the parameters do; each sample is converted from the depth of the stream to the grid and back with Config::convert_sample; the grid is 8 bit with full scale 255 or 16 bit with full scale u16_max
error_line: error: CODE: MESSAGE, one line on standard error, where CODE is usage, unsupported, bad_input, partial_frame, broken_pipe or stage_failed

exit_codes_table.means: every input frame was processed and written, or --describe printed its answer
stage_failed: the output could not be written for a reason other than a closed pipe
usage: a bad or missing option, a parameter or a layer given twice, a layer with an empty path
unsupported: a depth the stage does not take, a parameter or a layer the stage does not have, a value the stage refuses
bad_input, partial_frame or broken_pipe: a failed read, input that ends inside a frame, a frame count other than --frames, a layer file that cannot be read or parsed, a reader that went away
exit_codes_table.table: the table's bad_input, partial_frame and broken_pipe

unpinned_paths.why: a write to standard output that fails for a reason other than a closed pipe; no test makes one, because it needs a device that differs between systems
a reader that closes the pipe while the stage writes; the convention's conformance tool exercises it, the rows of this file do not

exit_codes.stderr: error: unsupported: depth-quantise takes no layers: `keys` is not one
error: usage: parameter `levels` given more than once
error: unsupported: depth 12 is not supported: depth-quantise takes 8, 16 or 32
error: unsupported: depth-quantise has no parameter `no_such_param`: it takes levels, u16_max, rounding, precision, clamp
error: unsupported: bad value for `levels`: `no-such-value` is not one of 8, 16
error: unsupported: bad value for `levels`: a keyed value is not taken on the command line; give a key file with --layer keys=PATH
error: unsupported: depth-quantise takes no layers: `no_such_layer` is not one
error: partial_frame: frame 1: the input ends inside a frame (3 of 4 bytes) after 1 whole frames
error: bad_input: the input holds 1 frames, but --frames says 2
